corrections.text: The article says the figure that differs between GitHub's February 4 post ("consumes one premium request") and its documentation (AI credits "based on the model used and the number of tokens processed") is unreconciled by the cited sources. GitHub's documentation page "What changed with Copilot billing (legacy)" says that before June 1, 2026 billing was premium-request-based and that "As of June 1, 2026, GitHub replaced request-based billing with usage-based billing"; the February 4 per-session figure describes the earlier model.

The article says Apple added "Claude, Codex and Claude Agent in Xcode 26.3". 9to5Mac reports that Apple introduced ChatGPT in Xcode 26, "followed by Anthropic's Claude" (no version given), and that Xcode 26.3 expanded both integrations through OpenAI's Codex and Anthropic's Claude Agent; Claude chat is not attributed to 26.3.

The article quotes Amit Kumar Jena as saying CIOs should "monitor agent activity through audit logs". Those words are InfoWorld's indirect report of his advice ("They should also monitor agent activity through audit logs ... he added"); his direct quotation in the piece is "set credit limits for individual projects".
